 Print this Article 
 View Comments Patriots offensive guard Ben Brown went down with a knee injury in Sunday's loss to the Packers. Danielle Parhizkaran/Globe Staff FOXBOROUGH — Following Sunday’s gruesome loss to the Packers , the New England locker room was quiet. As a result, as players were getting dressed, veteran safety Kevin Byard couldn’t help but overhear a conversation between teammate Craig Woodson and a reporter. 
 Woodson was asked about the Patriots’ near-catastrophic run of injuries over the course of the season, and if there was a breaking point for a team that lost more key players in Sunday’s 45-27 defeat . 
 “It’s pro football, man,” said Byard quietly as he continued to get dressed next to Woodson. 
 Woodson listened to Byard, and waited a second before replying with a shrug. 
 “At the end of the day, we’ve got to play football,” he said softly. “Regardless of who we’ve got. Who we don’t have. I mean, we’ve got to play.” 
 Related : Rob Gronkowski ends Patriots Hall of Fame induction weekend with a verbal Gronk spike: ‘This is my home’ No one in the New England locker room is going to make excuses, but it’s becoming evident that when you write the story of the 2026 Patriots, it’s going to be told in athletic tape and bandages. The only time they’ve been completely healthy this season was for the first quarter-plus of the opener against the Seahawks. Then, A.J. Brown went down with a high ankle sprain , and it’s been a parade of health problems ever since. 
 Get Point After Get exclusive analysis and insight on the Patriots and the NFL, delivered to your inbox on weekdays during the season. Enter Email Sign Up Sunday brought more of the same. With Brown, Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson , Alijah Vera-Tucker, and Mike Onwenu already sidelined, there was a steady run of players to the medical tent throughout the afternoon against Green Bay. Left tackle Will Campbell (knee), left guard Ben Brown (knee), cornerback Carlton Davis (knee), special teamer Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) were among those who were unable to finish. Additionally, tight end Cameron Latu looked like he got banged up on a second-half kick return. 
 “It’s football, man. This is football,” said veteran right tackle Morgan Moses, echoing Byard. “It doesn’t matter about the injuries. Obviously, you can sit there and say it’s affected us, but we believe in every man in this locker room when their number is called.” 
 “We play a physical game, with 100 percent injury risk,” said defensive tackle Milton Williams. “I feel like we’ve been dealing with [this] all year. So people ain’t gonna feel sorry for us if we’re dealing with injuries. I feel like we’ve had guys go out early in the year [that] we’re still dealing with. 
 “We’ve got to figure it out,” he added. “Nobody’s going to talk about the injuries. They’re just going to say, ‘We play the New England Patriots.’ We’ve just got to continue to put our best foot forward.” 
 Patriots backup guard Walter Rouse stands over an injured Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' loss to the Packers on Sunday. Danielle Parhizkaran/Globe Staff The Patriots are heading into an uncertain week. They’ll head to Germany for next Sunday’s date with the Lions, which means they’ll have to find a way to wash off the stink of Sunday’s loss faster than usual, all while dealing with the logistical challenges that come with playing overseas. 
 And while New England is scheduled to get some key players back sooner rather than later, there’s also the matter of Tuesday’s trade deadline to consider . Would the Patriots be inclined to make a move to shore up some positions of need, particularly running back, where there’s some uncertainty around the short-term future of both Stevenson and Henderson? 
 “We’ve got to control what we can control, and that’s playing football and going out there and displaying something that we feel good about,” Moses said when asked about how guys should handle the trade deadline. “And I think that’s the No. 1 priority.” 
 Regardless, with the bye week set for later this month, veteran receiver Mack Hollins seemed to indicate that with the imminent trade deadline, the self-scouting process should start a little early for some players. 
 Related : ‘It was just crazy’: Patriots’ Christian Gonzalez torched by Packers’ Matthew Golden and Christian Watson “You are what you put on tape,” the wide receiver said while standing by his locker. “Like, this is who we are this week. And if there’s guys on this team that are OK with that, I’m sure there’s 31 other teams they could go to maybe, and they could live like that. 
 “We’re trying to get stuff done. But this week, we just got our ass kicked. And if you’re not willing to come to work [Monday] and Tuesday and Wednesday and get on that plane and work all this week, then you’re probably not meant for this team.” 
 Ultimately, Williams and the rest of the roster are well aware of the gravity that comes with a week like this one. It’s not only a matter of flushing the ugly defeat, but having the mental toughness needed to get through the next 10 days. 
 How they respond — individually and as a group — could define the 2026 season. 
 “We’re going to find out a lot about our team after a game like this, with the deadline and all the other noise,” Williams said as he headed for the door. “We’re going to figure out the type of guys, the type of men we’ve got on this team, and just continue to find ways to improve. Continue to find ways to improve. 
 “And hopefully, we can get healthy.”
